card.line: Lebanon is a mountain region north of Israel, famous for its tall cedar trees, which the Bible uses for building the temple and for word pictures.

moments.title: Part of the promised land
moments.text: God tells Israel to leave Horeb and go to the land He promised, reaching to Lebanon and the great River Euphrates. Later He says He Himself will drive out the people of the Lebanon hill country.

moments.title: Cedar for the temple
moments.text: Solomon asks Hiram of Tyre to send cedar, cypress, and algum logs from Lebanon. He knows Hiram's servants are skilled at cutting timber there, and the temple will be great and wonderful.

moments.title: A palace of Lebanon wood
moments.text: Solomon builds the House of the Forest of Lebanon, with four rows of cedar pillars holding up cedar beams. His carriage is also made from Lebanon timber.

moments.title: Cedars for the second temple
moments.text: After the exile, the people pay workers from Sidon and Tyre to bring cedar logs from Lebanon to Joppa by sea. Cyrus king of Persia had authorized this.

moments.title: Cedars brought low
moments.text: Isaiah says the Day of the LORD will come against the proud, including the lofty cedars of Lebanon. Only the LORD will be exalted.
